question.text: In 1999, this large territory became a separate territory from the Northwest Territories.
question.clue: Although not a province, this Canadian territory is the newest, having been created in 1999 as a territory for the Inuit peoples.

swap.text: During the capture of the capital of this province, James Wolfe died on the Plains of Abraham. Despite the victory, this Canadian province still maintains its French roots.
swap.clue: One group in this polity kidnapped two government officials during the October Crisis.

question.text: MacDonald's two terms as prime minister saw the Red River and North-West Rebellions, both launched by this Metis Indian, the founder of Manitoba who was executed in 1885.
question.clue: This man was captured with the Cree Chief Poundmaker during the Battle of Batoche, and he appointed a tribunal which sentenced Thomas Scott to death.

swap.leadin: A 1950s government led by this party saw Minister of Housing Harold Macmillan lead a construction boom and Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden support a coup d'etat in Iran.
swap.text: Name this British political party, which defeated the Labour Party of Clement Attlee in 1951 elections.
swap.clue: A foreign secretary from this party issued a statement supporting a "national home" in an Ottoman area.

question.text: This British major general died after being shot three times during the Battle of the Plains of Abraham. This "Hero of Quebec" was memorialized in a painting by Benjamin West.
question.clue: This man's second-in-command, Robert Monckton, was wounded in a battle that paved the way for George Townshend to accept the surrender of a French colonial stronghold.

swap.text: This French explorer sailed across the Atlantic, down the St. Lawrence River, named Canada, and founded Montreal while looking for the Kingdom of Saguenay ("SA-gay-nay"), but only found quartz and iron pyrite.
swap.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

question.text: After de Gaulle's proclamation, this Canadian prime minister said that "Canadians do not need liberating." This leader formed the Royal Commission on the Status of Women while serving as Prime Minister from 1963 to 1968.
question.clue: This politician claimed "Canadians do not need to be liberated" in response to the "Vive le Quebec Libre" speech another man gave at Expo 67.

swap.text: When asked how he would address the crisis, this Canadian Prime Minister replied "Just watch me" and later invoked the War Measures Act.
swap.answerHtml: Pierre Trudeau [prompt on “Trudeau”; do not accept or prompt on “Justin Trudeau”]
swap.clue: This leader oversaw removing British authority through patriation, which also introduced the Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

question.leadin: Louis Montcalm led French forces at this battle, which was the site of a Benjamin West painting depicting The Death of General Wolfe.
question.text: Name this battle during the French and Indian War, which was followed up by the bloodier Battle of Sainte-Foy.
question.answer: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
question.clue: It resulted in the death of both commanders: for the French, the Marquis de Montcalm, and for the British, James Wolfe.

swap.text: The SNC-Lavalin affair is causing problems for this party in the 2019 election, and could help other parties, such as the Conservatives or the NDP win. This is the party of Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Canada [accept Parti libéral du Canada]
swap.clue: A request to dissolve parliament by a leader of this party was refused by Governor-General Julian Byng in 1926.

question.text: In the 1970s, this Canadian city demolished the nearby village of Africville which had been settled by several generations of Black refugees. Africville didn't receive aid from a 1917 explosion after the SS Mont-Blanc collided with the SS Imo in this city's harbor.
question.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

swap.leadin: Cuthbert Grant and his men won the Battle of Seven Oaks in this modern-day province.
swap.text: Name this province where Grant and his men killed Robert Semple and defeated the Hudson's Bay Company. A later rebellion in this province ended with the arrival of the Wolseley Expedition.
swap.clue: It is home to a lake where Black, Deer, and Hecla islands can be found near the town of Gimli and the source of the Nelson River, while its town of Brochet is on the east side of Reindeer Lake and York Factory and Churchill sit on its shore with Hudson Bay.

question.text: The Thule people, who spread east from Alaska and replaced the Dorset, were the ancestors of this ethnic group which now forms the majority of the populations of Nunavut and Greenland.
question.answerHtml: Inuit [accept Inuk; prompt on (but correct) Eskimo; antiprompt on Kalaallit; antiprompt on Inuktitut; antiprompt on Iñupiaq; do NOT accept or prompt on “Innu” or “Yupik”] (The Innu are a Cree-speaking Algonquian people whose traditional lands confusingly border the southernmost extent of Inuit in Labrador.)
question.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

swap.text: Canadian infantry troops under Julian Byng stormed Hill 145 at this World War I battle, losing thousands of men but earning respect from the British as a fighting force.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Vimy Ridge [prompt on the Battle of Arras]
swap.clue: This battle began on Easter Monday 1917 as part of the Second Battle of Arras.

question.leadin: A group led by Queen Yagowania, the Erie people, were completely wiped out during this series of wars.
question.text: Name this series of wars of expansion that a Native American confederacy fought to gain access to supplies of its namesake trade good. This series of wars was ended by the Treaty of La Grande Paix.
question.clue: The Iroquois defeated the Huron in this series of wars sparked by competition for the fur of a certain animal. These wars ended with the signing of the Great Peace of Montreal.

swap.leadin: This man exited office amidst backlash over a trade deal negotiated by his Finance Minister, William Stevens Fielding.
swap.text: Name this first Francophone Prime Minister of Canada, a Liberal from Quebec who settled the Manitoba Schools question.
swap.clue: This replacement of Charles Tupper created his nation's "tin pot" navy when he signed the Naval Service Bill.

question.text: St. Laurent was defeated by this Conservative, who controversially ended Canada's domestic fighter jet industry.
question.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

swap.leadin: A motorcade transported Nathan Cirillo's body down the "Highway of Heroes" in the aftermath of this event, which happened two days after Martin Couture-Rouleau rammed two soldiers with his car.
swap.text: Identify the location in Ottawa where, on October 22, 2014, Michael Zehaf-Bibeau exchanged gunfire with security personnel adjacent to a caucus room.
swap.answerHtml: Parliament Hill [or Centre Block; prompt on Canadian Parliament building or similar answers]

question.leadin: The Sadlermiut ("sah-hleer-mee-YOOT") were long theorized to be a vestige of this culture because they used stone tools to hunt walruses.
question.text: Name these people who lived in the Canadian Arctic before gradually being replaced by the Thule ("THOO-lee") and eventually disappearing around 1500 CE.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.leadin: This man worked with the Baring Brothers to secure financial backing for a railroad that connected Halifax to Windsor.
swap.text: Name this publisher of the Novascotian and Morning Chronicle who accused local politicians of stealing over 30,000 pounds from the public treasury, then was acquitted in a landmark 1835 trial affirming the freedom of the press in Canada.
